quote: There is no exclusion for Excluded Assets anywhere in the Bill of Sale... While APA § 10.12 provides that the APA controls in the event of a conflict, the same section also states that "each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its specific subject matter." The specific subject matter of the Bill of Sale is the conveyance of assets; one could argue the Bill of Sale's own definition governs what was conveyed... Alternatively, and more cleanly, replace the entire § 1.1(b) definition with: "Purchased Assets" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.1 of the Purchase Agreement.
reason: The memo addresses the Bill of Sale definition of 'Purchased Assets' ('used or held for use in the Business'). It points out that the definition neither carves out the Excluded Assets nor cross-refers to the APA. It explains the risk that the Albany facility and the HOLLIS trademark could be conveyed, and it ties that risk to the Bill of Sale controlling its subject matter under APA § 10.12. It recommends adding 'other than the Excluded Assets' or adopting the APA definition by reference, which together satisfy the revision recommendation.
